# Appendix A. Security Code Review Checklist

Developers use this checklist to self-review each merge request before submitting it. Tick each item that applies to the change; an item that cannot be ticked must be fixed, or explained in the merge request, before merging. The Security Reviewer uses the same checklist as the minimum scope of the security evaluation. Record significant findings as issues in the application's Git repository.

## Governance and Secure Development Lifecycle

- [ ] Does the feature have written, approved security requirements that this change meets?
- [ ] If this change adds a new data flow, integration or trust boundary, is the threat model updated?
- [ ] Does the change follow the reviewed architecture, using approved frameworks only?

## Authentication, Credentials and Sessions

- [ ] Does authentication use the approved identity provider and standard flows, with no custom scheme?
- [ ] Are failed logins logged, throttled or locked out, with no user enumeration?
- [ ] Do admin or privileged functions require MFA?
- [ ] Does the change add any default credentials, test accounts or seed users that could reach production?
- [ ] Are tokens stored securely, short-lived, rotated, and revoked on logout?

## Authorization and Access Control

- [ ] Is every new function protected by a server-side role or policy check?
- [ ] Does the change add a role or service account that needs to be added to the access review?

## Input Validation, Output Encoding and Injection

- [ ] Is every new input validated on the server with an allow-list, and not only in the app?
- [ ] Are all SQL, SQLite and SAP calls parameterized, with no string-built queries?
- [ ] Is all output encoded by the framework, with no Html.Raw / loadHtmlString / innerHTML on untrusted data?
- [ ] Are URLs, file paths, redirects and commands built with safe APIs and allow-lists?

## API and Integration Security

- [ ] Is data from SAP, vendors or other APIs validated before use, with timeouts and capped retries?

## Cryptography and Data in Transit

- [ ] Does all traffic use HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation left on?
- [ ] Does the change use only approved algorithms, a secure RNG and constant-time comparison?
- [ ] Are new keys stored in Key Vault / Keystore, with an owner and rotation plan?

## Data Protection and Privacy

- [ ] Does the change add new personal or sensitive fields, and are they classified and protected?
- [ ] Is every new personal data field needed, documented with a purpose, and covered by retention?
- [ ] Are reads and exports of personal data logged so a breach can be scoped?

## Secrets and Configuration

- [ ] Does the change contain any hardcoded credential, key, token or connection string?
- [ ] Did the secret scanner pass on this merge request?

## Error Handling and Exceptional Conditions

- [ ] Are error responses generic, with stack traces and internal details only in server logs?
- [ ] If anything in this change throws, does the code deny access and leave data consistent?

## Logging, Monitoring and Alerting

- [ ] Could any new log line, print or crash report contain a secret or personal data?

## File Upload and File Handling

- [ ] Are uploads checked for size, magic bytes and pixel count on the server, and are images re-encoded?

## Flutter Mobile Application Security

- [ ] Are tokens stored only in flutter_secure_storage, never in SharedPreferences or files?
- [ ] Is any sensitive data cached on the device, and if so is it encrypted and wiped on logout?
- [ ] Do new sensitive screens block screenshots and hide app-switcher previews?
- [ ] Does any new API host need adding to the pin set, with a backup pin?
- [ ] Is any biometric check bound to a Keystore/Keychain key rather than a boolean?
- [ ] Are deep links verified and validated, WebViews locked down, and native channel inputs checked?
- [ ] Is the release build obfuscated, signed with the production key, and free of debug features and extra permissions?
- [ ] If the app is High risk, are root/tamper detection and server-verified attestation in place?

## Supply Chain and Third-Party Components

- [ ] Are new or upgraded packages vetted, maintained and free of known vulnerabilities?
- [ ] Does the dependency scan pass with no unaddressed high or critical findings?
- [ ] Are lock files committed and updated, and does the build use locked restore?

## Source Control, Environments, Change and Deployment

- [ ] Is this change going through a reviewed merge request into a protected branch?
- [ ] Is the change linked to a change record with impact assessment and test evidence?
- [ ] Are debug features, test endpoints and API docs disabled for production?

## Security Testing and Code Review

- [ ] Are there tests for the security behavior of this change (unauthenticated, wrong role, other user's data, bad input)?
- [ ] Has the author run gitleaks, the analyzers and the dependency scan, and attached the results?

## Operations, Vulnerability Management and Incident Response

- [ ] Does this change close a security task, and is the task updated?
